system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation / reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at 20% of price (AUD 4.8m). | A materially higher cap (e.g. 50% / AUD 12m), or robust W&I insurance with an adequate seller retention; separate uncapped/specially capped regimes for excluded categories. | **Reject 20% as the sole recourse cap.** It is inadequate for a AUD 24m acquisition with concentrated contract, debt, IP and data-risk exposure. |
| **SPA-N-002 De minimis & basket** | AUD 25k de minimis; AUD 250k deductible basket, with only excess recoverable. | Lower de minimis and a tipping basket, or at least preservation of all claims once threshold is met; aggregation of related claims. | **Seek AUD 10k–15k de minimis and a tipping basket (or lower deductible basket), with aggregation.** The proposed thresholds can exclude recurring or related operational losses. |
| **SPA-N-003 General claims time limit** | General claims expire 18 months after Completion; Seller says limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least 24 months for general warranties, with longer tailored periods for tax, IP, privacy/data, employment and other identified risks. | **Extend general survival to 24 months and expressly separate special categories.** Eighteen months may not reveal annual-cycle, contractual, regulatory or latent issues. |
| **SPA-N-004 Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties subject to the same 20% cap and 18-month limit as general warranties. | Title, capacity, authority and ownership warranties uncapped (or at least capped at 100% of price) and surviving substantially longer, preferably limitation-period based. | **Reject.** Buyer must have full-value, durable recourse if it does not receive valid, unencumbered ownership of 100% of the shares. |
| **SPA-N-005 Fraud carve-out** | Broad limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions purportedly apply to all Claims; no express fraud carve-out is identified. | An express carve-out preserving all remedies for fraud, fraudulent concealment, wilful misconduct and deliberate/reckless misrepresentation; no cap, threshold or time-bar for fraud. | **Insert an express, non-excludable fraud carve-out.** Seller should not obtain contractual protection for dishonest conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the entire data room, Accounts, registers and public records, plus specific disclosures. | Specific, fair disclosure against identified warranties, with enough detail to identify the nature and scope of the exception and its consequences; no blanket data-room/public-record disclosure. | **Delete or sharply limit general disclosure.** A document dump does not fairly disclose a risk or allow the Buyer to assess it. |
| **SPA-N-007 Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer/advisers or discoverable from data room/public records. | Exclusion only for the Buyer’s actual, documented knowledge of the precise facts and resulting breach, held by named deal-team individuals; no constructive knowledge or adviser imputation. | **Reject “discoverable” knowledge and broad adviser knowledge.** It improperly converts diligence limitations into warranty exclusions. |
| **SPA-N-008 Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; considers consent addressed upon delivery of written consent, despite no final consent or evidence conditions are met. Bluefen represents about AUD 3.6m / 30% FY26 revenue. | Bluefen’s unconditional and effective consent, with all conditions satisfied or waived, as a Completion condition; long-stop/termination right and no adverse amendment or loss of contract. | **Make effective Bluefen consent a Buyer-benefit CP.** Loss or impairment of a 30% revenue customer is a fundamental value risk. |
| **SPA-N-009 Riverlark facility** | Approx. AUD 3.2m remains outstanding; security release to be provided after Completion. | Debt repaid at or before Completion from Seller proceeds, with simultaneous irrevocable payoff evidence and releases of all Company/security obligations. | **Require payoff and releases as Completion deliverables, not post-Completion promises.** Buyer must acquire a debt-free, cash-free Company free of Riverlark security. |
| **SPA-N-010 Employee bonuses** | AUD 420k conditional Completion bonuses are omitted from the funds flow; no treatment of payroll tax, super or other on-costs. | Seller bears/settles bonuses and every related employment cost, or purchase price is reduced/escrowed for the fully loaded amount; clear treatment in funds flow and accounts. | **Add a specific indemnity and Completion adjustment/holdback for fully loaded bonus liabilities.** They are transaction-triggered liabilities that should not become Buyer costs. |
| **SPA-N-011 Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment issue; AUD 180k remains open and no payment receipt or confirmatory assignment is available. | A specific, uncapped or appropriately high indemnity for all ownership, assignment, payment, infringement and remediation risk concerning Ironquay/SOW3 materials; evidence of cleared payment and valid assignment before Completion. | **Expand the indemnity and require documentary cure.** The Buyer may otherwise not receive clear ownership of material development IP. |
| **SPA-N-012 Export/privacy incident** | Seller characterises the incident as preliminary and not expected to be material; investigation is incomplete and no determination of access, scope or notification obligation exists. | Completion-condition/right to defer pending investigation, full remediation and notifications as required; specific indemnity for all pre-Completion incident liabilities, costs, claims and regulatory action. | **Do not accept the general regime alone; require a specific indemnity and investigation/response plan.** The unknown access and notification position creates potentially material regulatory and reputational exposure. |
| **SPA-N-013 Sandbar renewals** | Three renewals total AUD 330k and are said to be ordinary-course operating costs; disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Full contract details and treatment as debt-like/working-capital or specific indemnity if non-ordinary, non-terminable or not properly accrued; no adverse commitments before Completion without consent. | **Require clarification and price/indemnity protection if the commitments are binding or unaccrued.** “Ordinary course” is unsupported by the disclosed facts. |
| **SPA-N-014 Category separation** | Seller seeks to apply general limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance provisions to all Claims, and labels positions “[STANDARD]” to discourage review. | Express separate regimes for general warranties, fundamental/title, tax, IP, specific indemnities, covenant breaches, Completion claims and fraud. | **Reject the universal limitations language and disregard the “[STANDARD]” label.** Category-specific risks require category-specific survival, caps and remedies. |
| **SPA-N-015 Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register showing Seller holds 100%; says this evidences title. | Independent title verification and Completion deliveries: current register, share certificates, executed transfers, board approvals, ASIC/company searches, lien/security releases and title warranty. | **Require independent verification and clean-title deliverables.** A seller-provided register alone does not establish unencumbered, transferable title. |
| **SPA-N-016 Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says tax and IP are settled under the general 20%/18-month regime. | Standalone tax covenant/indemnity, tax warranties and longer tax survival (generally through the applicable assessment/limitation period); separate IP warranties/indemnities with appropriate caps and survival. | **Reject settlement under the general regime.** Tax and IP liabilities can be discovered late and may exceed the general warranty cap. |
=== END ADVICE ===
